newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PARLT BEGINS SECOND READING OF DRAFT BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PARLT BEGINS SECOND READING OF DRAFT BUDGET.

text.p: The Czech parliament began debating the second reading of the 1997 draft budget on Wednesday, with deputies promising a raucous discussion before an expected vote later in the week.

The government's fifth straight balanced budget draft proposes revenues and expenditures each totalling 549.1 billion crowns next year, after a 1996 balanced budget plan which forecasts a revised total of roughly 491 billion crowns.

The budget is expected to be approved by the parliament, though the two coalition partners of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) have demanded minor changes before giving their support to the draft.

Karel Machovec, one of four opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) who crossed the floor to vote with the government to allow approval of the legislation in the first reading told Reuters, said the party's caucus had to decide what tack it will take in the vote.
But, he added: "I expect quite a stormy debate over the budget, but in the end a peaceful vote."
The coalition lost its majority in the Chamber of Deputies in the general election last spring, winning 99 of 200 seats, making every vote for final budget approval crucial.
Junior coalition partner Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) has 13 votes in parliament while the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL), the other coalition member, has 18 seats.
A third and final reading of the budget cannot come sooner than 48 hours after the second reading is approved, but only minor changes can be introduced then.
